$comment: Mutation arms cutting the types of package anyparse.runtime. Format and rules: docs/testing.md, Declared arms.

arms.name: M-PARSE-MEMO-REPLAY-OFF
arms.note: a `@:memo` rule never replays a recorded run, so every `(`-led alternative re-parses the operand it shares with its siblings and a paren nest costs 2^depth

arms.name: M-PARSE-MEMO-STASHED-SKIP
arms.note: a run handed a pending trivia stash is not recorded, so a nest whose operands follow a line break (`(a) ->` newline `(`) re-parses 2^depth times

arms.name: M-SKIM-GAPS-COUNTED
arms.note: a brace inside a string, a comment or a regex counts, so a skipped body ends at a quoted `}`

arms.name: M-SKIM-NEVER
arms.note: no body is ever skipped: the declarations read is a full parse, and a body the grammar cannot read hides the module's declarations

arms.name: M-SKIM-BRANCH-DEPTH
arms.note: a directive branch that does not return to the depth its region opened at is balanced across branches, so a body whose branches each open a brace ends past its own close

arms.name: M-SKIM-REGION-LEFT-OPEN
arms.note: a body may end inside a directive region it opened, so the members after it are read as part of the region

arms.name: M-SKIM-OUTER-REGION
arms.note: a directive of a region opened before the body is taken for one of the body's own

arms.name: M-SAMEITEMS-LENGTH-ONLY
arms.find: for (i => item in a) if (item != b[i]) return false;
arms.note: two arrays of one length count as the same whatever they hold

arms.name: M-SORTED-OFFSETS-LOWER-BLIND
arms.note: the search never moves past an offset below the range, so the first offset of the array answers

arms.name: M-SORTED-OFFSETS-UPPER-BLIND
arms.find: return lo < sorted.length && sorted[lo] < to ? sorted[lo] : -1;
arms.note: an offset at or past the upper bound answers, so ArgumentValues reads the written type of the NEXT declaration

arms.name: M-DROPPED-SEP-KEPT-REHOMED
arms.note: a comment after a separator the writer keeps is moved into the element, in front of the separator

arms.name: M-DROPPED-SEP-BLOCK-REHOMED
arms.note: a block comment after a dropped separator moves into the element, changing a layout the first write already settles

arms.name: M-BOM-NOT-CARRIED
arms.note: the written text never gets the source byte-order mark back, so a whole-file write strips it

arms.name: M-CHAIN-OWN-COMMENTS-UNTAKEN
arms.note: a chain operator leaves its own-line comments on the stash, so they drift into whatever its operand parses next

arms.name: M-COMMENT-RUN-BLOCKS-SPLIT
arms.note: block comments joined into one trailing slot each start a line of their own, so `b, /* c */ /* d */` breaks apart
